title: Marguerite and the Ledger
premise: In the winter of 1921, in a mountain republic dissolving under an armistice nobody signed willingly, Ivo Hartwell carries a courier's satchel and ten years of practiced silence. When the season's last bridge closes, she is stranded in Marguerite, a river town where an old landlady's ledger records debts, favors, and names that could damn the negotiators on both sides. To deliver her evidence past three checkpoints before the armistice ceremony, Ivo must decide whether memory is a burden to smuggle or a weapon to spend — and whether belonging can be built in a place she was only passing through. She delivers the ledger at cost: the town burns its own history to save it, and Ivo stays, becoming the keeper of what remains.
about_author: Juniper Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing displaced-persons records from interwar Europe before turning to fiction. They write about borders, paperwork, and the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Bell
chapters.summary: Ivo arrives in Marguerite with forged transit papers and a sealed dispatch, intending to cross the bridge north by morning. The ferryman warns her the ice will close the crossing within days. POV: Ivo. Beat: wary competence masking exhaustion; the reader feels her decade of calculated silence pressing down.

chapters.title: A Room at the Widow's
chapters.summary: Snow blocks the pass; Ivo takes a room from Odile Marchand, whose guesthouse ledger tracks every debt in town going back thirty years. Odile reads Ivo's papers too carefully. POV: Ivo. Beat: unease braided with unexpected warmth — the first room in years that smells like someone else's life.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Ivo glimpses entries naming officers now sitting at the armistice table, including the man who signed her brother's death warrant. She realizes Odile's book is evidence worth more than her dispatch. POV: Ivo. Beat: cold recognition; duty and revenge begin to blur.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Ivo tests the southern tollhouse with her official papers and learns the garrison has orders to detain all couriers until after the signing. A young sergeant lets her go for a debt his father owes Odile. POV: Ivo. Beat: relief curdling into fear — the whole town is entangled in her mission now.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile confronts Ivo: she knows what the girl saw in the ledger. She offers the pages in exchange for one entry — her son's name, struck from a collaboration list — restored before the record leaves town forever. POV: Odile. Beat: grief weaponized into negotiation; two keepers of secrets recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Ice shears the bridge span; the road out is gone until spring. The armistice signs in eleven days. Ivo is trapped with her evidence, her enemy's name, and a town watching her too closely. POV: Ivo. Beat: claustrophobic dread; every ally becomes a potential informer.

chapters.title: Bread and Interrogations
chapters.summary: Garrison Captain Veyra arrives to billet in the guesthouse, charming and thorough, asking each lodger where they were the night the archive in the capital burned. Ivo lies well; Odile lies better. POV: alternating Ivo/Odile. Beat: a duel of hospitality; terror conducted over soup.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counts Rivers
chapters.summary: Ivo befriends Tomas, Odile's grandson, who maps the frozen river's channels in a school notebook — including a shallows crossing usable on foot in hard frost. POV: Tomas. Beat: innocence as accidental strategy; Ivo feels the first pull of belonging she cannot afford.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Chapel Steps
chapters.summary: Ivo copies the damning pages and moves them through the chapel, where Father Anselm runs a quiet line of smuggled letters. Veyra searches the sacristy while Ivo kneels in plain sight. POV: Ivo. Beat: faith as cover and genuine refuge; the copy survives by inches.

chapters.title: Veyra's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ivo discovers Veyra keeps her own book of favors and threats — power running on the same currency as Odile's memory. The captain offers Ivo immunity for the original ledger, revealing she knows about the armistice-table names. POV: Veyra. Beat: seduction of safety; corruption offering itself as mercy.

chapters.title: What Ivo Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the night Ivo's brother was taken, and the silence she kept to survive — the silence she has been carrying ever since. She understands Odile's price is not blackmail but resurrection. POV: Ivo (past and present). Beat: the wound opens; motive clarifies from duty to reckoning.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: At the tavern, the townsfolk debate surrendering the ledger to buy the garrison's goodwill. Odile stands and reads three entries aloud — debts owed by the very men negotiating peace. The room turns. POV: ensemble, anchored by the blacksmith Brannoc. Beat: collective courage kindling; memory becomes communal armor.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Mill
chapters.summary: The miller, terrified for his sons, sells the plan of the chapel route to Veyra. Father Anselm is detained; the copied pages are seized — but they are decoys Ivo planted. POV: miller's wife, guilt-ridden. Beat: betrayal and its terrible tenderness; the noose tightens around the wrong necks.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Ice Road
chapters.summary: Ivo and Tomas attempt the river shallows at night with the true ledger sewn into her coat. The ice groans; halfway across, a patrol lamp sweeps the bank. Tomas's knowledge of the channels saves them. POV: Ivo. Beat: white-knuckle peril; trust placed in a child becomes the story's purest act.

chapters.title: The Cost of Crossing
chapters.summary: Tomas falls through a soft patch; Ivo pulls him out but the soaked ledger's ink begins to run. They shelter in a hunting hut where Ivo dries page by page over coals, reading names aloud so Tomas will know why it matters. POV: Ivo. Beat: intimacy forged in crisis; the ledger becomes testimony, not cargo.

chapters.title: Armistice Eve
chapters.summary: They return to find Marguerite under curfew and Odile arrested for harboring a courier. Veyra offers a final trade: Odile's freedom for the ledger and Ivo's confession. POV: Odile, in her cell. Beat: despair sharpened into resolve; the keeper chooses the record over herself.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Before the signing delegation passes through town, Ivo walks into the square and reads the ledger's armistice-table entries aloud to the assembled garrison and townsfolk, daring Veyra to silence her publicly. The crowd takes up the names, hundreds of voices. POV: Ivo. Beat: the climax — private silence broken into public memory; power confronted with its own receipts.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints Fall
chapters.summary: Sergeant, priest's flock, and crowd become Ivo's checkpoints in reverse: the town itself escorts her and the ledger to the delegation's train, Veyra's authority dissolving as her own ledger of favors is read back to her soldiers. POV: Veyra. Beat: corruption unmasked not by violence but by accounting; the captain's elegant machinery eats itself.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: On the station platform, Ivo places the ledger and her dispatch in the hands of a neutral delegate. The armistice is signed with the record attached; her brother's signatory is named, investigated, undone. POV: Ivo. Beat: hollow triumph — justice arrives, but it tastes like ash and snow.

chapters.title: Ashes in the Archive
chapters.summary: Retaliating officers burn the guesthouse; Odile, freed in the chaos, saves only the ledger's empty twin. The town mourns its paper memory. POV: Brannoc. Beat: grief and defiance intertwined; a community learning that memory lives in people, not pages.

chapters.title: A New First Entry
chapters.summary: Spring opens the bridge. Ivo, offered safe passage home, instead writes the new ledger's first line: Odile's son's name, restored. The town begins dictating its debts and graces anew. POV: Odile. Beat: quiet restoration; the price paid and the promise kept.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Marguerite
chapters.summary: Years later, Ivo trains a new generation of couriers to carry testimony, and teaches Tomas the ledger hand. When travelers ask who keeps the town's memory, they are told: the woman who stayed. POV: Ivo. Beat: resolution — silence transformed into stewardship; belonging earned, at last, by staying.
